subject: Burst contour & live-streaming SLA — follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — throughput contours & streaming needs

Thanks for a productive call earlier, Sarah — appreciate you walking through the Kestrel traffic patterns. Short recap + our immediate asks so we can size a pilot and produce a short SLO proposal.

Quick summary of what we heard (please correct any mistakes):
- Steady-state baseline: ~70–90 requests/sec (QPS) for standard conversational queries, median tokens/request ~280.
- Recurring daily peak (batchy): bursts that ramp up to ~900–1,200 QPS that last 90–300 seconds; typical burst shape is fast ramp (~10–30s) + 3–4 minute plateau + 2–3 minute decay.
- Token mix: median ~280, peak 95th ~520 tokens/request during heavy-search batches.
- Streaming: live agent-assist product — 50–80 concurrent live streams during normal hours, with worst-case 180 concurrent during promotions; per-stream per-token ingress ~5–12 tokens/sec once active.
- Latency goals: P95 end-to-end (user-facing) target ~150ms for short completions; streaming per-token tail <25ms if possible.
- Retention/cache: KV-cache reuse expected for session continuity for up to 30 minutes; we need to confirm cache hit-rate assumptions.

Immediate asks from our side (can you please provide):
1) The raw token/QPS distribution sample for your busiest 24-hour window (CSV or similar) — we can then produce token/sec heatmaps.
2) Clarify burst duration percentiles (we noted 90s–300s but want p50/p90/p99).
3) Confirm whether streaming sessions allow dropping to a lower-quality model during extreme load (is graceful degradation acceptable?).

I've attached a blank CSV template (kestrel_workload_snapshot.csv) — if you can paste a small sample there we will run it through our sizing tool and return a recommended initial capacity and a candidate canary plan by EOD Friday.

Next internal step: Ben/Tessa — I'll consolidate the pilot sizing proposal after Sarah replies with the CSV.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — throughput contours & streaming needs

Thanks Marissa — attaching a short sample extract (kestrel_workload_snapshot.csv) and inline clarifications below.

Clarifications:
- Burst windows: p50=120s, p90=260s, p99=420s (the very long ones are usually promotional events).
- Steady-state: median QPS ~82; typical off-peak ~18–25 QPS.
- Tokens/request distribution: median 295, p95 ~540, p99 ~900 (we see long-form requests during research workflows).
- Streaming: baseline concurrent streams 55, peak concurrent streams 180 (peak tends to coincide with burst windows and lasts 2–6 minutes). Streams are bi-directional; we need per-token latency under 30ms to avoid perceived audio lag in our agent UI.
- Degradation: yes, acceptable — we can tolerate a fallback to a slightly smaller model for streaming (not for critical billing flows).

Open items for Redwood: can you confirm whether KV-cache is sticky per-session (session affinity) or global across routing? That impacts the initial cache sizing.

Sarah
VP Product, Kestrel.ai

Attachments: kestrel_workload_snapshot.csv (sample, 42 rows)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@kestrel.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — throughput contours & streaming needs — internal sizing draft

Looping internal sizing notes into the thread so Sarah has context; attaching a short SLO summary (redwood_slo_summary.pdf) with conversion math. High level plan and assumptions below — want your read on whether this lines up with the sample CSV Sarah provided.

Assumptions pulled from the CSV and the call:
- Avg tokens/request (steady): 295 tokens -> avg token/sec per req (non-streaming) depends on model latency; assume 20ms/token decode on the candidate quantized 13B variant under steady batched ops.
- Steady-state: 82 QPS * 295 tokens = ~24k tokens/sec steady.
- Peak burst plateau: 1,100 QPS * 295 tokens = ~324k tokens/sec for 3 minutes (we model a 10–30s ramp).
- Streaming: 180 concurrent streams * 10 tokens/sec = 1,800 tokens/sec (additionally KV traffic and incremental small-model inferences for assistant context).

Initial capacity recommendation (pilot):
- Dedicated pool mapping: 2 x 80GB A100 equivalent machines for steady baseline + autoscale to 8 machines to cover burst plateaus (canary schedule to validate autoscale behavior).
- Model variant: start with quantized 13B (balanced perf/cost); have a plan to fall back to 6B-quant for streaming-only degradation path.
- Batching: aggressive windowing for steady-state; short batch windows (5–10ms) for low-latency paths; streaming uses single-token micro-batches (<5ms).
- KV/cache: prefer session-affinity (sticky routing) for better hit rates; if Kestrel cannot commit, prepare a slightly higher cache size to compensate.

SLO suggestions to propose to Kestrel:
- Non-streaming p95 server-side decode latency target = 100ms (gives ~150ms end-to-end after client/network).
- Streaming per-token server-side p95 = 15–25ms (we can hit low-20s with micro-batching + optimized kernels).

Next actions:
1) Marissa: send Sarah a concise pilot MOP (mutual action plan) with the proposed capacity and timeline.
2) Tessa: prepare an autoscale test plan to exercise a 300s plateau at 1,100 QPS in our staging fleet.
3) Ben: produce a cost delta between staying on quantized-13B vs forced fallback to 6B during peak plateaus.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the sample and the clarifications, Sarah — that p99 burst length and the p99 tokens/request help a lot. Condensed next steps and a proposed pilot timeline below.

Condensed next steps (pilot MOP):
1) Redwood will provision an initial Dedicated pilot: 2x steady machines + autoscale to 8 machines (timeline: 2 business days to stand up).
2) Redwood will run an autoscale/stress canary in staging mimicking a 300s plateau at 1,100 QPS (Tessa to own — target window next Tue).
3) Kestrel to confirm: session-affinity for KV-cache (yes/no) by EOD Monday; if no, we'll size cache + routing conservatively.
4) Legal/Proc: Marissa will send a short MOU for the pilot (no commitment beyond pilot) — expected sign within 48 hours; deal contact Rahul for procurement.

Pilot success criteria (suggested):
- Sustain 1,000 QPS plateau for 3 minutes with p95 E2E <200ms for non-streaming and streaming per-token p95 <30ms.
- No more than 2% request error rate under plateau; KV hit-rate >= 40% for session-affinity mode.

Can you confirm the acceptance criteria and sign off on the MOP? If yes, I'll schedule a kickoff and send a short DocuSign for the pilot MOU.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.
Marissa
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
